name: Easy One-Pot Miso Soup

instructions.primary_message: Combine water, kombu, and bonito flakes in a large saucepan and bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce to a bare simmer and cook for 5 minutes. Remove from heat, let cool for 5 minutes, then strain through a fine-mesh strainer. Discard solids.

Return broth to a medium saucepan and set over low heat to keep warm, but not boiling. Place a fine-mesh strainer in broth and add miso paste to the strainer. Use the back of a spoon to press paste through strainer into broth. Discard any large grains that don't pass through.

Add tofu, wakame, mushrooms, and cockles (if using), and allow to cook without boiling until ingredients are warm and wakame has rehydrated, about 5 minutes. Garnish with scallions (if using) and serve immediately.

schema_metadata.keywords: Asian, miso, miso soup, quick, soup

description: Traditional miso soup uses second dashi—an intense soup stock made from the leftover sea kelp and shaved bonito from first dashi. This quick version of miso soup achieves a full flavored soup base without the need to make two separate batches of stock.
notes:
Optional or for serving: 227 g firm silken tofu, cut into 1.5-cm cubes (optional); 14 g dried wakame seaweed (1/4 cup, optional); 113 g fresh mushrooms, sliced if necessary (such as honshimeji, namako, or shiitake, optional); A handful of small live cockles (optional); 4 whole scallions, thinly sliced (optional)

Optional substitutions: white miso paste → red miso paste

Notes: Kombu and katsuobushi can be found in any Japanese market or in the international section of most well-stocked supermarkets. For best results, use real kombu and katsuobushi. Alternatively, you can use powdered dashi mix. Follow instructions on the package.
author: J. Kenji López-Alt
